intent.raw_query: Banff hiking and lakes, $2800 couple, 6 days, July 2027, from Calgary

experiences.name: Lake Louise Lakeshore & Plain of Six Glaciers Hike
experiences.description: Hike the iconic trail from the turquoise shores of Lake Louise up to the Plain of Six Glaciers teahouse, offering breathtaking views of Victoria Glacier and surrounding peaks. One of the most rewarding hikes in the Canadian Rockies with stunning alpine scenery at every turn.

experiences.name: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks Exploration
experiences.description: Visit the legendary Moraine Lake, arguably the most photographed lake in Canada, and hike the Rockpile Trail for panoramic views of the Valley of the Ten Peaks. Arrive early via the Parks Canada shuttle to secure access and witness the vivid blue glacial waters at their most magical.
experiences.location: Moraine Lake Road, Lake Louise Corridor

experiences.name: Banff Gondola & Sulphur Mountain Summit Hike
experiences.description: Ride the Banff Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres for 360-degree views of six mountain ranges, or hike the 5.5 km trail up for free and take the gondola down. Explore the restored Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station and enjoy the sweeping panoramas over Banff townsite.

experiences.name: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Trail
experiences.description: Walk the dramatic Johnston Canyon trail along suspended catwalk ledges carved into the canyon walls, leading to the stunning Lower and Upper Falls. Extend the hike to the Ink Pots — seven cold mineral springs with vivid turquoise and green pools set in an open meadow with mountain views.

experiences.name: Icefields Parkway Self-Drive & Peyto Lake Viewpoint
experiences.description: Drive one of the world's most scenic highways, the Icefields Parkway, stopping at Peyto Lake — a wolf-head shaped turquoise lake viewed from Bow Summit, the highest drivable point in Banff National Park. Stop at Bow Lake, Mistaya Canyon, and Weeping Wall along the way for a full day of immersive Rocky Mountain nature.
experiences.location: Icefields Parkway (Highway 93 North), Banff National Park

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 14:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and meal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00 on Flight AC. Collect baggage and take the Banff Airporter shuttle (~$60 CAD one-way, book in advance for best price) to Banff town. Journey takes about 1.5–2 hours. Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along Banff Avenue to get your bearings. Browse the free Cascade Gardens and enjoy views of Cascade Mountain.
day_by_day.evening: Explore downtown Banff on foot. Walk to the free viewpoint at the Bow River Bridge for golden-hour mountain reflections. Grab a budget dinner on Banff Avenue.

meals.lunch: Pack snacks or grab a quick bite at Calgary Airport (Tim Hortons or Subway, ~$10–12 CAD)
meals.dinner: Nourish Bistro on Bear Street – plant-forward, budget-friendly bowls and wraps (~$15–18 CAD). Alternatively, pick up groceries at IGA Banff for self-catering options to save money throughout the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Stop at IGA Banff or Nesters Market after check-in to stock up on breakfast items, snacks, and trail food for the week – this is the single biggest budget-saving move of the trip. Purchase a Parks Canada Day Pass (~$10.50 CAD/person/day) or a Discovery Pass (~$72.25 CAD/person for the full year – worth it for 6 days) at the park gate or online before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Trail – Depart the hotel by 08:00 to beat crowds and secure parking (free before 8 AM at the trailhead lot, or take the Roam Transit Bus Route 8X from Banff for ~$6 CAD round-trip). Walk the dramatic suspended catwalk ledges carved into the canyon walls to the Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). The canyon is cool and shaded – perfect for a warm summer morning. Optional extension to the Ink Pots (11 km round-trip total) for colourful mineral springs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by early afternoon. Visit the free Banff Visitor Centre to plan the week. Walk up to the free Surprise Corner viewpoint for iconic views of the Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel framed by mountains. Explore the Hoodoos Trail (free, 4.8 km round-trip) along the Bow River – a short, easy nature walk with unique geological formations.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Central Park along the Bow River. Watch for elk, which frequently graze near town at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at lodge – oatmeal, fruit, and coffee from groceries purchased yesterday (~$3 CAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Johnston Canyon – sandwiches, trail mix, and fruit from IGA (~$5 CAD)
meals.dinner: Banff Ave Brewing Co. – try their pub-style burger and beer deal or share appetizers (~$18–22 CAD). Look for their daily specials board.

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers for the canyon – it stays cool inside even on warm days. Bring a rain jacket as afternoon showers are possible. Trail is paved and accessible. Go early – Johnston Canyon is one of Banff's most popular trails and gets very crowded by 10 AM in summer.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks – This requires an EARLY start. Moraine Lake Road is accessible ONLY by shuttle or on foot/bike in 2027 (private vehicles restricted). Book the Roam Transit shuttle from Banff (Route 10, departs ~06:30–07:00, ~$10 CAD each way) or the Parks Canada shuttle from Lake Louise Park & Ride well in advance at reservation.pc.gc.ca. Arrive at Moraine Lake by 07:00–07:30. Hike the Rockpile Trail (1.5 km, easy) for the legendary Valley of the Ten Peaks panorama – arguably Canada's most iconic view. Then hike the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km round-trip) along the impossibly blue glacial waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the shuttle to Lake Louise village (~15 min). Walk to the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise lakeshore (free) and enjoy the turquoise views. Begin the Plain of Six Glaciers Hike – hike from the lakeshore up to the teahouse (14 km round-trip, moderate, ~500 m elevation gain). The teahouse serves basic food but is pricey; pack your own lunch instead.
day_by_day.evening: Return by shuttle to Banff. Rest your legs – this is a big hiking day.

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared breakfast at lodge before 06:00 departure – energy bars, bananas, peanut butter toast (~$3 CAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on the Plain of Six Glaciers trail – wraps, cheese, nuts, dried fruit (~$6 CAD)
meals.dinner: Melissa's Missteak on Lynx Street – a Banff institution with hearty portions; try the soup and sandwich combo or daily special (~$16–20 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: Shuttle reservations for Moraine Lake are MANDATORY and sell out weeks in advance – book as soon as possible. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and plenty of water (2L+). Start the Lake Louise hike no later than 13:00 to comfortably complete it and catch the return shuttle. Wear broken-in hiking boots – the Plain of Six Glaciers trail has rocky terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Icefields Parkway Self-Drive Day – Rent a car for the day (~$60–80 CAD via Enterprise or Budget in Banff, book ahead) or join a budget group tour. Depart Banff by 08:00 and drive north on Highway 93 (Icefields Parkway). First stop: Herbert Lake (free, 30 min) – a calm reflective lake perfect for mountain photography. Continue to Bow Lake (free) – a stunning turquoise glacial lake with easy lakeshore walking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to Peyto Lake Viewpoint – hike the Bow Summit Trail (2.2 km round-trip, easy) to the famous wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake overlook, one of the most spectacular views in the Rockies. Continue to the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre (exterior free; Athabasca Glacier walk-on is free from the road pullout – skip the expensive glacier tour to stay on budget). Drive back south along the Parkway, stopping at Sunwapta Falls (free) and Athabasca Falls (free) if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff. Enjoy a quiet evening with a walk to Vermilion Lakes (free) for a stunning sunset over the Three Sisters mountains – one of the best free experiences in Banff.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at lodge – eggs, toast, coffee (~$3 CAD)
meals.lunch: Packed road-trip lunch eaten at Bow Lake picnic area – sandwiches, apples, trail mix (~$6 CAD)
meals.dinner: Bear Street Tavern – wood-fired pizza in a casual setting; share a pizza between two for ~$15–18 CAD per person. Great value for the quality.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up the rental car's gas tank in Banff before departing – fuel on the Parkway (Saskatchewan Crossing) is significantly more expensive. The Parkway is 230 km one-way to Jasper; today's itinerary covers the southern highlights and returns, roughly 200 km round-trip. Carry a paper map or download offline maps – cell service is limited on the Parkway. Return the rental car by 18:00 to avoid extra charges.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Lakeshore & Plain of Six Glaciers Hike (dedicated full-day version if not completed on Day 3, or alternative: Sulphur Mountain Hike from Banff). If doing Sulphur Mountain: hike the Sulphur Mountain Trail (11 km round-trip, 655 m elevation gain, free) starting from the Banff Upper Hot Springs parking lot – skip the expensive gondola and hike up instead. At the summit, enjoy 360° panoramic views of six mountain ranges and walk the free Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station boardwalk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Sulphur Mountain. Reward yourself with a soak at the Banff Upper Hot Springs (~$16.50 CAD adult entry – a worthwhile budget splurge). Lockers and towel rental available on-site. Alternatively, cool off with a free swim at Johnson Lake (10-minute drive or Roam Transit accessible) – a warmer, calmer lake great for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the free Fenland Trail loop (2 km, flat, forested) near the train station – great for spotting beaver and waterfowl at dusk. Pick up groceries for a self-catered dinner to save budget.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at lodge – yogurt, granola, fruit (~$3 CAD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Sulphur Mountain summit – enjoy the view while eating wraps and snacks (~$5 CAD)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at lodge – pasta with jarred sauce, salad, bread from IGA (~$8 CAD for two people). Save the restaurant budget for the final night.

day_by_day.notes: The Sulphur Mountain hike is strenuous – start by 09:00 to avoid midday heat and afternoon thunderstorms. Bring trekking poles if available. The hot springs are open 09:00–23:00 daily in summer. Johnson Lake is a locals' secret for swimming and is free – a great alternative to the busy town beach. Check the Banff weather forecast each morning at weather.gc.ca as afternoon thunderstorms are common in July.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Banff – take a peaceful walk along the Bow River Trail (free, flat, paved) from Central Park toward the Bow Falls. Bow Falls is free to visit and offers a dramatic cascade with mountain backdrop – a perfect final memory. Browse the Saturday Farmers Market (if applicable) or window-shop on Banff Avenue for last-minute souvenirs. Pick up locally made items like maple syrup or Rocky Mountain soap as affordable gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (store luggage at reception if needed). Take one final stroll through town. Depart for Calgary Airport via Banff Airporter shuttle (book return in advance, ~$60 CAD). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the shuttle journey plus airport check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary Airport. Reflect on an incredible 6-day adventure through one of the world's most beautiful national parks.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared final breakfast at lodge – use up remaining groceries (~$3 CAD)
meals.lunch: Crave Mountain Grill or a deli sandwich from the IGA deli counter for a quick, affordable farewell Banff meal (~$12–15 CAD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Calgary YYC (Tim Hortons, A&W, or Freshii for budget options ~$12–15 CAD)

day_by_day.notes: Book the return Banff Airporter shuttle well in advance – it fills up on summer Mondays. Check out time is typically 11:00; confirm with the lodge. Use any remaining Parks Canada pass value today. Total estimated trip budget per person (excluding flights and accommodation): ~$350–450 CAD for 6 days, including food (~$30–35/day), transport (~$120 shuttle + $40 Roam Transit + $40 car share), park pass (~$72), and one hot springs entry (~$17).

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Calgary Airport at 14:00, collect luggage and pick up rental car. Drive the scenic 1.5-hour Trans-Canada Highway route to Banff (approx. 130 km). Check in to Banff Mountain Lodge, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation stroll along Banff Avenue to get your bearings, browse local shops, and visit the Banff Visitor Centre to pick up trail maps and park passes.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely sunset walk along the Bow River Trail near the hotel, then head to dinner in downtown Banff.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or at Calgary Airport — grab a bite at one of the terminal cafés
meals.lunch: Grab a casual bite en route or at a Canmore stop — try Communitea Café in Canmore for a mid-range sandwich or bowl (~CAD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Elk + Avenue Kitchen & Bar in downtown Banff — relaxed atmosphere, Canadian comfort food, mains CAD 22–35. Great introduction to local cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Parks Canada Discovery Pass at the Banff Visitor Centre or online before arrival to save time at park gates. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and the drive from Calgary can be tiring. Confirm rental car has a full tank for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early start to beat the crowds — depart hotel by 7:00 AM for Moraine Lake (45-minute drive). Explore the legendary Moraine Lake and hike the Rockpile Trail for the iconic Valley of the Ten Peaks viewpoint. Follow with the Lakeshore Trail (3.4 km return) along the brilliant blue shoreline. Note: Moraine Lake Road requires a Parks Canada shuttle reservation or park-and-ride from Lake Louise — book in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 15 minutes to Lake Louise. Walk the Lake Louise Lakeshore Trail (4 km return) and continue up to the Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (14 km return total, ~4–5 hrs) for sweeping glacier views. Alternatively, if energy is lower after Moraine Lake, simply enjoy the lakeshore and Agnes Lake Trail as a lighter option.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff by 6:30–7:00 PM. Shower and relax before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack a hearty breakfast from a Banff bakery the night before — Wild Flour Bakery opens at 7:00 AM for fresh pastries and coffee (CAD 10–14)
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (if completing full hike) — soups, sandwiches, and baked goods with a glacier backdrop (~CAD 18–25). Pack snacks as backup.
meals.dinner: The Bison Restaurant & Terrace in Banff — locally sourced Rocky Mountain cuisine, mains CAD 28–42. Try the Alberta bison or wild salmon.

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake shuttle tickets sell out weeks in advance — book via the Parks Canada reservation system before your trip. Start at Moraine Lake first as it gets extremely crowded by 9:00 AM. Bring layers; temperatures at elevation can be 8–10°C cooler than in town even in July.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Johnston Canyon (20-minute drive west of Banff). Walk the suspended catwalk trail through the dramatic limestone canyon to the Lower Falls (2.7 km return, easy) and Upper Falls (5.4 km return, moderate). Arrive by 8:00 AM to enjoy the canyon before tour groups arrive. The canyon is cool and shaded — perfect for a warm morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Johnston Canyon, drive a further 20 minutes west along the Bow Valley Parkway to visit Ink Pots — a series of vivid cold-water springs in an open meadow (add 11.6 km return hike from Johnston Canyon trailhead, ~3 hrs). Alternatively, return toward Banff and spend the afternoon at Vermilion Lakes for a peaceful lakeside walk and wildlife watching (elk and beavers frequently spotted).
day_by_day.evening: Ride the Banff Gondola up Sulphur Mountain at golden hour (gondola runs until 9:00 PM in summer). Enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges at 2,281 metres. Walk the Skywalk boardwalk to the historic Cosmic Ray Station. Watch the sunset before riding back down.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab coffee and oatmeal at Whitebark Café in Banff before departing (CAD 12–16)
meals.lunch: Pack a trail lunch — sandwiches and snacks from Nesters Market grocery store in Banff. Picnic at the Ink Pots meadow or Vermilion Lakes (~CAD 15–20 self-catered)
meals.dinner: Sky Bistro at the top of Sulphur Mountain (gondola summit) — elevated Canadian dining with mountain views, mains CAD 30–45. A memorable mid-range splurge worth the setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Banff Gondola online in advance for a small discount and to guarantee your preferred time slot (evening slots are popular in summer). Gondola ticket ~CAD 65–75 per adult. Bring a warm layer for the summit — even in July it can be breezy and cool at 2,281 m.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day self-drive along the iconic Icefields Parkway (Highway 93 North). Depart Banff by 7:30 AM. First major stop: Bow Lake (approx. 1 hour from Banff) — walk the easy lakeshore path with views of Crowfoot Glacier reflecting in the turquoise water. Continue north to Peyto Lake Viewpoint (Bow Summit, 2,088 m) — hike the 1.6 km return trail to the famous wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake overlook, one of the most spectacular vistas in the Rockies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north to the Columbia Icefield area (approx. 1 hr from Peyto Lake). Stop at the Athabasca Glacier viewpoint and walk to the glacier toe on the free public trail. Optional: book the Ice Explorer glacier tour (~CAD 60–70) for a guided walk on the ice. Visit the Glacier Skywalk (~CAD 35) for glass-floored views over the Sunwapta Valley. Begin the return drive south along the Parkway, stopping at Sunwapta Falls and Athabasca Falls (both short, easy walks to dramatic waterfalls).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Banff by 7:00–7:30 PM. Relax and enjoy a casual dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or Coyotes Southwestern Grill in Banff before departure (CAD 14–20)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Nesters Market — eat at Peyto Lake or Bow Lake picnic areas. Alternatively, Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre has a cafeteria (~CAD 18–25)
meals.dinner: Tooloulou's Restaurant in Banff — casual Cajun-inspired menu, lively atmosphere, mains CAD 20–32. Great for a relaxed end to a long driving day.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your gas tank before leaving Banff — fuel on the Icefields Parkway is extremely limited and expensive. The total round-trip drive is approximately 380 km. Bring snacks, extra water, and a printed/downloaded offline map as cell service is sparse along the Parkway. Book Columbia Icefield experiences online in advance if desired.

day_by_day.morning: A slightly more relaxed morning — sleep in or enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Mid-morning, head to the Banff Upper Hot Springs (10-minute drive up Sulphur Mountain Road) for a soak in the naturally heated mineral pool at 1,585 m elevation with mountain views (~CAD 16–18 per adult). This is a perfect recovery morning after the long Icefields Parkway day.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hot springs, hike the Sulphur Mountain Trail on foot (5.5 km one-way, 655 m elevation gain, ~2–3 hrs up) as an alternative to the gondola — take the gondola down for free if you hike up. Or opt for the moderate Tunnel Mountain Trail (4.8 km loop, ~1.5 hrs) directly from downtown Banff for panoramic views over the Bow Valley — a perfect half-day hike accessible right from town. Spend late afternoon exploring the Banff townsite: browse the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies or walk the Bow Falls trail.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a nicer dinner on your second-to-last evening, then enjoy a final stroll along Banff Avenue for local craft shops and ice cream.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at the hotel or Evelyn's Coffee Bar in Banff — known for excellent espresso and breakfast wraps (CAD 12–18)
meals.lunch: Block Kitchen & Bar in Banff — casual sandwiches, burgers, and salads, great mid-range lunch spot (CAD 18–26)
meals.dinner: The Grizzly House in Banff — a Banff institution since 1967, famous for fondue and wild game. A fun, unique dining experience, mains CAD 30–50. Book ahead as it fills quickly.

day_by_day.notes: Banff Upper Hot Springs is open daily in summer, typically 9:00 AM – 11:00 PM. Towel and swimsuit rentals available on-site. The Tunnel Mountain hike is one of the best accessible hikes from the townsite with no car required — ideal if you want a break from driving.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — rise early for one last Banff experience. Drive to the Two Jack Lake and Lake Minnewanka area (15 minutes from town). Walk the easy Lake Minnewanka Lakeshore Trail (easy, go as far as you like along the 28 km trail — even 3–4 km return is stunning). The lake is the largest in Banff National Park and offers dramatic mountain reflections. Watch for bighorn sheep along the road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Banff by 11:30 AM. Check out of Banff Mountain Lodge (standard checkout 11:00 AM — request late checkout if possible). Pack the car and do any final souvenir shopping on Banff Avenue. Grab a farewell coffee and treat. Begin the 1.5-hour drive back to Calgary Airport, allowing plenty of time for car return and check-in (recommend arriving at YYC at least 2.5 hours before departure).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary Airport or overnight in Calgary if flight is the following day.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the hotel — make the most of included breakfast if offered, or visit Bear Street Tavern for a hearty eggs benedict or pancakes (CAD 16–22)
meals.lunch: Quick and satisfying farewell lunch — Nourish Bistro in Banff for fresh, wholesome bowls and wraps (CAD 16–24), or grab road-trip snacks from Nesters Market for the drive
meals.dinner: If departing late or staying in Calgary: dinner at Model Milk in Calgary — creative farm-to-table Canadian cuisine in a converted dairy building, mains CAD 28–42

day_by_day.notes: Confirm hotel checkout time in advance and arrange luggage storage if needed for the morning activities. Return rental car with a full tank to avoid fuel surcharges. Lake Minnewanka is also excellent for wildlife spotting at dawn — keep eyes open for deer, bighorn sheep, and occasionally black bears along the road (maintain safe distance). Leave Banff no later than 1:30 PM for a comfortable airport arrival with buffer time.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight AC arrives at 14:00. Travel from Calgary International Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge (~1.5 hours by private transfer). Settle into your luxury suite and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeured transfer from Calgary Airport to Banff Mountain Lodge. Upon check-in, enjoy a welcome amenity and orientation with the concierge to plan the week ahead. Take a leisurely stroll along Banff Avenue to acclimate to the mountain air and explore the charming town centre.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Bow River trail near the lodge, followed by a relaxed first dinner at the hotel or a top Banff restaurant to ease into the trip.

meals.lunch: Grab a premium bite at Calgary Airport's Maple Leaf Lounge if available, or pack a gourmet snack for the road
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eden Restaurant at Rimrock Resort – Banff's only CAA Five Diamond restaurant, offering an intimate fine-dining experience with contemporary Canadian cuisine and an award-winning wine list. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private luxury transfer (e.g., Brewster Express or a private SUV service) from Calgary Airport in advance. Ask the concierge to book all restaurant reservations for the week upon check-in. The evening is intentionally light to allow for rest after travel. Banff town centre is a 5-minute walk from most premium lodges.

day_by_day.morning: Banff Gondola & Sulphur Mountain Summit Experience: Begin the day with an early ride on the Banff Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain at 2,281 metres. Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat the crowds and enjoy 360-degree panoramic views of six mountain ranges and the Bow Valley. Walk the 1 km boardwalk ridge to the historic Sanson's Peak Meteorological Station. The warm summer weather makes this an ideal clear-sky morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and visit the Banff Upper Hot Springs for a restorative soak in the naturally heated mineral waters with stunning mountain views – a perfect way to relax after the morning elevation. Follow with a curated visit to the Whyte Museum of the Canadian Rockies for cultural depth and local history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a patio overlooking Cascade Mountain, followed by a refined dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: In-lodge breakfast at Banff Mountain Lodge or a gourmet spread at Juniper Bistro with sweeping valley views before heading to the Gondola
meals.lunch: Sky Bistro at the top of the Banff Gondola – a premium dining experience at the summit with panoramic Rockies views and seasonal Canadian menu
meals.dinner: The Bison Restaurant & Terrace – celebrated for its Rocky Mountain cuisine, locally sourced bison, wild game, and an extensive craft cocktail and whisky selection. Cozy lodge-style ambiance.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Banff Gondola tickets in advance online to secure an early time slot. Gondola opens at 8:00 AM in July. Bring a light layer as summit temperatures can be 5–8°C cooler than town even in summer. The Upper Hot Springs is a 5-minute drive from the Gondola base station.

day_by_day.morning: Lake Louise Lakeshore & Plain of Six Glaciers Hike: Depart early (7:00 AM) by private vehicle or Roam Transit to Lake Louise (45 minutes from Banff). Begin the iconic hike along the turquoise lakeshore, then ascend the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail (14 km round trip, moderate difficulty). The trail climbs through ancient moraines and offers breathtaking close-up views of the Victoria Glacier and surrounding peaks. The warm 25°C weather makes for ideal hiking conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and stop for refreshments at the historic Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse (open July–September, cash only) perched dramatically on the moraine. Return to Lake Louise and explore the iconic Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise grounds and lakeshore at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff for a well-earned luxury dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast box arranged by the lodge concierge the night before – enjoy it en route or at the Lake Louise lakeshore
meals.lunch: Plain of Six Glaciers Teahouse – a bucket-list experience; enjoy homemade soups, sandwiches, and baked goods at 2,135 metres with glacier views
meals.dinner: Walliser Stube Wine Bar at the Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise (if staying late) OR back in Banff at Saltlik Steakhouse – a premier AAA-grade Alberta beef steakhouse with an exceptional wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Start as early as possible to secure parking at Lake Louise or use the Parks Canada shuttle from the Park & Ride. Wear sturdy hiking boots and bring trekking poles for the upper moraine section. The teahouse is cash only and does not accept reservations – arrive before 1 PM to avoid a wait. Total elevation gain ~365 metres. National Parks Pass required – ensure it is purchased in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Moraine Lake & Valley of the Ten Peaks Exploration: Depart by 6:30 AM to access Moraine Lake (mandatory reservation system or private guided access in peak season). Hike the Rockpile Trail for the legendary viewpoint over the impossibly blue lake framed by the Valley of the Ten Peaks – arguably Canada's most iconic vista. Continue along the Lakeshore Trail for a peaceful walk along the water's edge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional upgrade: Book a private canoe on Moraine Lake for an exclusive on-water perspective of the Ten Peaks. Return to Banff by early afternoon and indulge in a luxury spa treatment at the Willow Stream Spa at the Fairmont Banff Springs – choose from a mountain-inspired body wrap, hot stone massage, or the signature Rockies ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner at one of Banff's finest establishments.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed lodge breakfast box to enjoy at Moraine Lake at sunrise – one of the most spectacular breakfast settings on Earth
meals.lunch: Moraine Lake Lodge dining room (for lodge guests or advance reservation) offering light lakeside lunches, OR a premium charcuterie and cheese picnic arranged by your concierge to enjoy on the lakeshore
meals.dinner: 1888 Chop House at the Fairmont Banff Springs – a legendary Banff institution offering prime Alberta beef, fresh seafood, and an extraordinary 700-label wine list in a grand castle-like setting

day_by_day.notes: Moraine Lake Road requires a Parks Canada reservation or use of an approved shuttle/tour operator – confirm access method well in advance as this is one of the most sought-after spots in Canada. Private guided tours with operators like Discover Banff Tours can secure access. Willow Stream Spa bookings should be made at least 2–3 days ahead. Weather at Moraine Lake can be cooler and windier – bring an extra layer.

day_by_day.morning: Johnston Canyon Waterfall Trail: Drive 25 minutes west of Banff to Johnston Canyon. Walk the dramatic suspended catwalk trail carved into the canyon walls, passing the photogenic Lower Falls (1.1 km) and Upper Falls (2.7 km). The warm summer conditions create spectacular mist and rainbow effects at the falls. Arrive before 9:00 AM for the most peaceful experience before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Icefields Parkway Self-Drive Scenic Journey: From Johnston Canyon, join the Icefields Parkway (Highway 93 North) – one of the world's most scenic drives. Stop at Bow Lake, Herbert Lake, and the unmissable Peyto Lake Viewpoint (a wolf-head-shaped turquoise lake surrounded by glaciers and boreal forest). Drive at a leisurely pace, stopping at every viewpoint. Optional: continue to the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre for a glacier walk experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Banff in the early evening. Enjoy a relaxing night with a premium dinner and reflection on the week's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the lodge before departure – request a full hot breakfast from the kitchen
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the lodge concierge – enjoy at Peyto Lake viewpoint or Bow Lake's stunning shoreline
meals.dinner: Maple Leaf Grille & Lounge in Banff – celebrated for its Canadian regional cuisine featuring Alberta beef, Pacific salmon, and locally foraged ingredients in a warm, upscale setting

day_by_day.notes: Rent a premium vehicle (e.g., luxury SUV) for the Icefields Parkway drive if not already arranged. Fill up on fuel in Banff before departing as gas stations are limited along the Parkway. The full Icefields Parkway to Jasper is 230 km one-way – today's itinerary covers the southern highlights and returns to Banff. Bring a camera with a wide-angle lens for Peyto Lake. National Parks Pass required for all stops.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in the Rockies – Sunrise at Vermilion Lakes: Wake early for a serene sunrise walk or private guided photography session at Vermilion Lakes, just minutes from Banff town. The still water perfectly mirrors the surrounding peaks and is one of the most tranquil and photogenic spots in the park. Watch for wildlife including elk, beavers, and osprey. Follow with a leisurely check-out from Banff Mountain Lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final curated experience: browse Banff Avenue's premium boutiques for Canadian artisan goods, visit the Cave and Basin National Historic Site (birthplace of Canada's national park system), or enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a local café. Private luxury transfer departs for Calgary International Airport (allow 2+ hours before flight).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Calgary or overnight extension if flights permit.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the lodge – request a special final morning spread. Alternatively, breakfast at Coyotes Deli & Grill for a celebrated Banff brunch experience
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Block Kitchen & Bar in Banff town centre – modern Canadian small plates and craft cocktails, perfect for a relaxed final meal before the drive to Calgary
meals.dinner: If departing late or extending in Calgary: dinner at MARKET Restaurant by Chef Michael Noble in Calgary – one of Alberta's top farm-to-table fine dining destinations

day_by_day.notes: Check-out is typically 11:00 AM – arrange a late check-out with the lodge in advance if your flight is in the evening. Store luggage with the concierge if you wish to explore after check-out. Allow a minimum of 1 hour 45 minutes driving time to Calgary Airport, and up to 2.5 hours to account for summer traffic. Tip: purchase a few bottles of local ice wine or Canadian whisky at the Banff liquor store as premium souvenirs before departure.

query: Banff hiking and lakes, $2800 couple, 6 days, July 2027, from Calgary
